convoLines.text: "Do you still sing? ...Sorry — weird question. I just realized I haven't heard anyone sing. I'm listening."
"Ha! The creek concerts. I've heard those. Keep going."
"Under my breath, when I'm working. Old songs from Hanoi, Vietnam. The words are half gone but the tune holds. Tunes outlast everything."
"Why do you ask? Still on whether you still sing."
"All right. Thank you for asking."
"I work alone. Nothing personal. ...It's a little personal."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Michelle always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Anyway — I should get back to it. Good talking, though."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"What are you hoping for? Not the big stuff. The small thing."
"God, yes. That's the dream now. Eight hours of not being afraid."
"A full night's sleep. Not safety, not answers — just eight hours where nothing needs me. That's my whole theology now. — or so they tell me."
"Don't laugh yet — Still on what you're hoping for."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Since Michelle died... I keep expecting to see Michelle at the fire. Stupid."
"Anyway — I should get going."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 4 days back. 'They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.'"
"I keep turning over the last thing Michelle said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"The fire feels smaller without Michelle. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
"Still on what's been happening. I mean it."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
You show them Serviceberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You wanted one full night's sleep — no waking up listening. Had it yet?"
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that personal stuff."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Michelle owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
You show them Serviceberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"You've been singing in the creek. Badly, by your own admission. Heard anything worth stealing yet?"
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that personal stuff."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Last time things were different. They always are." "They took Lena — Cooking With Teeth, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Right. Go on, then."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 7 days back. 'You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.'"
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
It's quiet at the hollow. Pietro doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"My part? I save the best bite for last and stay ready."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on what's been happening."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"Can I tell you something? I'm practicing what I would say if I ever saw my family again. I haven't told anyone."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Funny thing: Still on their secret."
"What's the worst thing you've done since the sky changed?"
No judgment in their face. "We're all doing math that doesn't add up. You're still here. That counts."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
You show them Serviceberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Don't tell anyone I told you. What's on your mind? That's my read."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "They took Pietro — The Pit, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"Same weather, different day. I keep notes."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Where are you from — originally? Before all this."
Nods slowly. "Columbus, Ohio. I'll remember that. Everybody's from somewhere that isn't here."
"Me? Columbus, Ohio. I still dream in its weather — rain on a tin roof, that specific smell. I wake up here and for a second I'm furious at the sky for the swap."
"Still on where you're from. ...sorry, lost it."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "The Pit. They just... took Pietro. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"This was good." They mean it.

deathBeat: d12: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Michelle Kozlov is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d12: 🕯️ Michelle Kozlov is dead — lockjaw. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
recoverHome: d13: That night, they bring Michelle home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
systemVoice: d12: SYSTEM: Codex and inventory overlay online.

d14: 📺 SYSTEM: "AUDIENCE EXPANSION! Your party cap is now FOUR! The people demanded bigger ensembles! Don't let us down!"
d14: 📺 SYSTEM: "A viewer sent this. A FAN. We checked. It is not dinner." A pause. "We checked twice. The fans are very insistent that you open it ON CAMERA."
d14: ⬢ SYSTEM: "Neural depth 66. I can hold more of you now — ability slots: 5."
d14: SYSTEM: Oh! It has a NAME. You all love names.
burialWindowSay: d12: ◈ The System files the name away with visible satisfaction. It has so few words for things that bleed. (+5 integration)
d13: That night, they bring Michelle home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
d15: You say a few words for Michelle. Not a ceremony — just: you were here, and someone noticed you leaving. (-3 trauma)
d15: You bury Michelle. A marker, of sorts. The village will know where. (+4 trauma)
